liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The Other One into Not Fade Away, Goin' Down The Road and Morning Dew is called epic; Space builds notably into The Other One, which follows with very hot playing [1][27][29]
- **Me And Bobby McGee** (2 reviews): Only Weir played acoustic on a few first-set songs, Bobby McGee among them; the set wasn't fully acoustic; Reviewer finds this Bobby McGee the most lifeless ever recorded, and the rest of the acoustic set little better [22][24]
- **The Boxer** (1 review): Joan Baez played The Boxer and a couple of other songs before the band joined her [23]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer says this Dark Star came after almost three years without one [27]
- **Banks Of The Ohio** (1 review): Jerry began on acoustic guitar but swapped to electric by the end of the first verse [28]
- **Playin' In The Band Reprise** (1 review): Second-set Playin' is fast and about fifteen minutes, with another jam and reprise after Terrapin [29]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Reviewer calls this a Shakedown version he always wanted to hear live [29]
- **Big Boss Man** (1 other source): Matt Kelly guests on Big Boss Man, which runs into Minglewood Blues [2]
- Matt Kelly sits in on C C Rider, and also on Big Boss Man and Minglewood [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-12-31 s0t01 Land Of A Thousand Dances**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t02 Do Right Woman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t03 The Boxer**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t04 Tunisian New Year**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t05 Me & Bobby McGee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t06 Bye Bye Love**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t07 Lucifer's Eyes**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]
- **gd81-12-31 s0t08 Children Of The 80's**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-12-31.143570.sbd.healy.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 38 songs; 248 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-12-31.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.96090.flac24**: soundboard; 35 songs; 247 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd81-12-31.acoustic.warren.14040.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 25 min; rated 3.54/5 by 13 [21]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears marginal quality like a mediocre audience tape: hiss, distortion and little presence [24]
- **gd1981-12-31.143571.sbd.healy.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 38 songs; 248 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended with a backstage pass he took, and says the night before had the same mix of acoustic and electric [22]
- Reviewer was backstage in Joan's entourage; she had been dating Mickey Hart for about eighteen months [26]
- Baez wasn't always asked to sing at Dead shows; Jerry in particular disliked the idea [26]
- It was the only four-set show this reviewer ever attended [28]
- Bill Graham fed the audience after the show; it was this reviewer's first Dead concert [30]
- Reviewer finds Joan Baez's singing somewhat overpowering at times, though less than Donna's can be [31]
- Joan Baez joins on the acoustic songs, including Bobby McGee, Bye Bye Love, Lucifer's Eyes and Banks Of The Ohio [1]
- Joan Baez sings on Roses, Beat It On Down The Line, Don't Ease Me In and Baby Blue; Matthew Kelly joins for Iko [3]
- Reviewer calls it the first two-verse Dark Star since the early 1970s and ranks the songlist among the best of the 80s and 90s [27]
- Uploader describes this as an upgrade over all earlier circulating copies [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-12-31.143570.sbd.healy.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Dan Healy and Joani Walker; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Paul Scotton; source: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony D5M (Dolby B)(TDK MA-R C90) [1]
- **gd1981-12-31.sbd.walker.scotton.miller.96090.flac24**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell UDXLII-S90) [3]. Also: Source is a Nakamichi 100 front-of-board to cassette master; a cassette patch fills a brief Goin' Down The Road gap [3]
- **gd81-12-31.acoustic.warren.14040.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [21]. Also: Reviewer owns an old cassette of the full set, which the CD copies he has seen lack [23]
- **gd1981-12-31.143571.sbd.healy.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Dan Healy and Joani Walker; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Paul Scotton; source: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony D5M (Dolby B)(TDK MA-R C90) [2]

claims.text: Only Weir played acoustic on a few first-set songs, Bobby McGee among them; the set wasn't fully acoustic
Reviewer attended with a backstage pass he took, and says the night before had the same mix of acoustic and electric
Joan Baez played The Boxer and a couple of other songs before the band joined her
Reviewer owns an old cassette of the full set, which the CD copies he has seen lack
Reviewer finds this Bobby McGee the most lifeless ever recorded, and the rest of the acoustic set little better
Reviewer hears marginal quality like a mediocre audience tape: hiss, distortion and little presence
Reviewer was backstage in Joan's entourage; she had been dating Mickey Hart for about eighteen months
Baez wasn't always asked to sing at Dead shows; Jerry in particular disliked the idea
Reviewer says this Dark Star came after almost three years without one
Reviewer calls it the first two-verse Dark Star since the early 1970s and ranks the songlist among the best of the 80s and 90s
The Other One into Not Fade Away, Goin' Down The Road and Morning Dew is called epic
Jerry began on acoustic guitar but swapped to electric by the end of the first verse
It was the only four-set show this reviewer ever attended
Second-set Playin' is fast and about fifteen minutes, with another jam and reprise after Terrapin
Reviewer calls this a Shakedown version he always wanted to hear live
Space builds notably into The Other One, which follows with very hot playing
Bill Graham fed the audience after the show; it was this reviewer's first Dead concert
Reviewer finds Joan Baez's singing somewhat overpowering at times, though less than Donna's can be
Joan Baez joins on the acoustic songs, including Bobby McGee, Bye Bye Love, Lucifer's Eyes and Banks Of The Ohio
Matt Kelly sits in on C C Rider, and also on Big Boss Man and Minglewood
John Cippolina guests on The Other One, Not Fade Away and Goin' Down The Road
Matt Kelly guests on Big Boss Man, which runs into Minglewood Blues
John Cippolina plays on Not Fade Away, along with the Other One and Goin' Down The Road

claims.song: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue
claims.text: Joan Baez returns for the encore Baby Blue after the Dark Star, Bertha, Good Lovin' set
Source is a Nakamichi 100 front-of-board to cassette master; a cassette patch fills a brief Goin' Down The Road gap
Joan Baez sings on Roses, Beat It On Down The Line, Don't Ease Me In and Baby Blue; Matthew Kelly joins for Iko
Uploader describes this as an upgrade over all earlier circulating copies
Notes list Iko Iko as opening the second electric set, marked as featuring Joan Baez
Show is laid out as an acoustic set, two electric sets, then a third electric encore set starting with Dark Star
